title: I updated my Control fan game "Panopticon": you now have to contain what you classify
author: supertweedo
selftext:
[https://supertweedo.itch.io/panopticon](https://supertweedo.itch.io/panopticon)

**What’s new**

* **Containment.** In the evening, every object you classified as anomalous goes down to the Panopticon. There are eight cells, each built to prevent something: a dark cell, a watched cell, a soundproof cell, a sealed cell, a restraint cradle, and the Fortified Units. Whatever set an object off in the test chamber, its cell has to stop.
* **Nights have consequences.** Every need you left uncovered becomes an incident overnight. It costs you in the Board’s evaluation, and the next shift starts with less containment integrity. Classifying takes little evidence; containing well means you actually tested the thing.
* **A second shift**, with four new objects: a class photograph from 1971, a music box, a hotel room key and a pocket watch. And the Board has started paying attention to your floor.

**The AI side of this update**

* Object needs are never written by hand. They’re derived from the reactions you can trigger in the test chamber, the same way the expected verdict is. A content test then runs an exhaustive search to make sure each day can be contained with zero incidents.
* The class photo is painted entirely in code (drawn in an offscreen viewport, then read back as a texture), so that a blurry child can turn to face the camera under the floodlights.
* I noticed the technician walking through a floodlight. Instead of just moving the path, Claude wrote a test that replays the walk and checks every part of the suit against the room’s geometry.
* The trailer above was made the same way: a scripted playthrough recorded with Godot’s Movie Maker, then cut and scored with ffmpeg.

Free, in the browser, about 20–30 minutes (desktop, mouse and keyboard): [https://supertweedo.itch.io/panopticon](https://supertweedo.itch.io/panopticon)

Unofficial, non-commercial fan game, not affiliated with Remedy Entertainment. Feedback welcome.
